- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop — increase downward forecast bias.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 70, adjust downward by 2–5% of forecast range.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum shifts — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast transitions.
- For 30d horizon, model often overfits recent volatility — reduce forecast sensitivity to last 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
